subject: Approval request: downtime makeup & service-credit ceiling for Acme Health pilot
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Approval request: downtime makeup & service-credit ceiling for Acme Health pilot

Team —

Quick summary: Acme Health (pilot customer) is asking us to accept a lower uptime threshold for their 90-day pilot window in exchange for a 20% pilot discount and an explicit maximum service-credit cap of 10% (they want firm compensation limits for budgeting). Their workload is highly bursty RLHF-style inference during scheduled windows, and they've asked us to "build in" tolerance for transient infra interruptions while they validate the integration.

Why this is non-standard: our standard commercial terms cap service credits at 15% and preserve the 99.9% uptime SLO for production. Acme is requesting we:
- Treat the pilot like a scoped pilot SLO of 98.5% uptime for the 90-day pilot period
- Limit cumulative service credits during the pilot to 10% of monthly fees
- Provide a written "makeup plan" that commits Redwood to prioritized incident response during pilot windows (on-call and weekly health checks)

Attachments: SLA_Makeup_Plan_v2.pdf (technical mitigations + on-call cadence) and Deal_Worksheet_Acme.xlsx (pricing / expected ARR motion).

Ask: I need an exec ratification (jonas or above) to accept the non-standard remedy and the 10% cap so we can finalize commercial terms with Acme by Monday. Legal (Lauren) — please confirm whether we can scope the modified SLO to the pilot without creating precedent in our standard master agreement. Tessa — confirm CSA/operations can meet the on-call commitments in the attached plan. Marissa — commercial perspective / risk acceptance.

If you prefer, I can redline a short amendment that limits the change to the pilot term only.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-29T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Approval request: downtime makeup & service-credit ceiling for Acme Health pilot

Karthik — thanks for the crisp write-up. A couple of quick clarifying items before I can recommend approval to revenue ops/finance: 

1) ACV and expansion motion: the attached worksheet shows $48k for the 3-month pilot and a committed P0 conversion target of $600k ARR if they go to prod within 9 months. Confirmed?
2) Why the 98.5% vs 99.0% ask? Is this purely to give them headroom for scheduled maintenance windows or are there known capacity constraints?
3) Do we expect any operational cost delta (e.g., reserved burst capacity) that should be reflected in the pilot price?

If finance signs off on the 10% cap and legal can gate the language to the pilot anniversary, I can push the deal forward with the commercial note that this is a one-off pilot concession tied to a conversion commitment.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Mid-Market Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-29T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Approval request: downtime makeup & service-credit ceiling for Acme Health pilot

Short operational note: we reviewed the workload profile with infra and the attached SLA_Makeup_Plan_v2 contains the operational commitments we can reasonably make for a 90-day pilot: 
- Dedicated maintenance blackout windows documented with customer (they accept short scheduled downtimes)
- Prioritized pager routing during customer pilot windows (Mon-Fri 06:00–20:00 PT)
- Weekly pilot health check calls and an assigned CS escalation lead

We can commit to the on-call and monitoring changes, but any guaranteed availability below our standard SLO must be scoped to the pilot and tied to the pilot fees and conversion milestone. Also — we recommend adding an automated failover to a secondary region as a mitigation; cost estimate included in Deal_Worksheet_Acme.xlsx.

Operationally okay from CS & Infra as long as finance accepts the proposed pilot economics.

—Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Health Legal <contracts@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-30T10:16:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Approval request: downtime makeup & service-credit ceiling for Acme Health pilot

Thanks — I reviewed the proposed amendment language. Legal position: we can limit the modified SLO and reduced service-credit cap to a defined 90-day pilot term, but two controls are required in the amendment: 
1) Non-precedent clause: explicit language that the pilot SLO and cap do not modify our master terms for any future agreements.
2) Sunset & review: the pilot amendment must expire automatically at the pilot end date and trigger a mandatory conversion review (no implied renewal of pilot remedies).

Also — the current makeup wording in SLA_Makeup_Plan_v2 is operationally fine but legally vague on "prioritized incident response." Please replace with specific commitments (escalation path, on-call windows, response/acknowledgement times).

I will prepare a redline and upload to the DocuSign link once commercial confirms the final numbers. If legal receives the signed pilot amendment with the controls above, we can accept the 10% cap for the pilot only.

—Lauren Bishop
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-30T16:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Approval request: downtime makeup & service-credit ceiling for Acme Health pilot

I reviewed the thread and attachments. I am willing to ratify the exception to permit a 98.5% pilot SLO with a 10% service-credit ceiling on two conditions: 
1) The amendment contains Lauren's non-precedent and sunset language (no changes to master terms).
2) Finance approves the limited cap given the expected conversion economics (Marissa, please confirm finance sign-off).

Assuming those two items are satisfied, consider this an executive approval to proceed and close the pilot contract. Karthik — finalize the redline with Lauren and send it to Acme for signature.

Jonas Weber
VP, Commercial
Redwood Inference
